title: The pig that nearly started a war
hook: A pig nearly started a war between America and Britain.
summary: In 1859 an American farmer shot a British-owned pig on San Juan Island, triggering a standoff of warships and soldiers that lasted twelve years with no death except the pig.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica / Wikipedia 'Pig War': pig shot 15 June 1859 on San Juan Island by Lyman Cutlar; pig owned by Hudson's Bay Company; only casualty was the pig.

US National Park Service, San Juan Island National Historical Park: joint military occupation until 1872; Kaiser Wilhelm I arbitration awarded the islands to the United States in 1872; Admiral Baynes declined to fight over the pig.

lines.text: A pig nearly started a war between America and Britain.
In eighteen fifty-nine, an American farmer shot it for eating his potatoes.
lines.caps: In *1859, | an American *farmer | *shot it for | eating *potatoes

lines.text: Soon, hundreds of American soldiers faced five British warships on the island.
The British admiral arrived, and refused to fight over a pig.
lines.caps: The British *admiral | *arrived, and | *refused to fight | over a *pig

lines.text: So both armies camped there for twelve years.
Then a German emperor settled it, and the island went to America.
lines.caps: Then a *German emperor | *settled it, | and the *island | went to *America

lines.text: The only death in the Pig War was the pig.
lines.caps: The only *death | in *the Pig War | was the *pig

post.caption:
A potato-eating pig took two empires to the edge of war. Cooler heads won.
Would you have backed down over a pig?
